newsitem.title: USA: Army opens misconduct case against top soldier.
newsitem.headline: Army opens misconduct case against top soldier.

text.p: An attorney for the U.S. Army's top enlisted soldier charged on Wednesday that his client was not getting a fair hearing to determine whether he will be court-martialed on charges of sexual misconduct.

Attorney Charles Gittins spoke on the first day of a hearing in the case against Army Sgt. Maj. Gene McKinney, who faces 18 charges of sexual misconduct and obstruction of justice involving three Army women and a female sailor.

McKinney, 46 and married, is the Army's top enlisted person. He has denied committing adultery with one of the women and propositioning the others in the latest chapter of a growing sexual harassment scandal that has rocked the Army.

"I think it's absolutely important that the soldiers know that their senior enlisted soldier is going to get a fair and impartial hearing to see if I am going to be court-martialed," McKinney told investigating officer Col. Robert Jarvis, who is overseeing the hearing at Fort McNair Army Base in Washington.

Gittins, McKinney's civilian lawyer, said the Army was treating the case "in a cavalier fashion" and demanded that Jarvis remove himself from the case because he had prematurely reviewed some of the evidence against McKinney.
Jarvis, who is not a lawyer but will recommend to superior officers whether or not McKinney should be court-martialed, said he would consider those and other defence motions.

McKinney is accused of adultery with one woman and propositioning three others. He is also charged with assault, indecent assault, making a threat, mistreatment of a subordinate and obstruction of justice.

The hearing officer will weigh the evidence and decide whether to proceed with a trial, change the charges or dismiss the case. Meanwhile, McKinney has requested that he be allowed to retire with an honourable discharge.
The case is the latest in a scandal involving adultery and sexual harassment in the military, including the rape of women recruits by Army drill sergeants.
